question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Feud
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Harmony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Feud" means a bitter, prolonged quarrel or conflict between two people, families, or groups, often lasting for a long time. (कटु झगड़ा/वैमनस्य)
◦ Example: The two families have been engaged in a bitter feud for three generations.

• Since a feud is a state of ongoing conflict and hostility, its antonym must denote peace and agreement — that is, "Harmony", which means a state of peaceful agreement and cooperation. (सामंजस्य/मेल)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Distrust (अविश्वास): A lack of trust or confidence in someone; this is close in meaning to feud, not opposite to it.

• Option 3: Unfriendliness: The state of not being friendly or amicable; this is a near-synonym of feud, not its antonym.

• Option 4: Destruct: To destroy or demolish; unrelated in meaning to the idea of conflict versus peace.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Feud": quarrel, vendetta, dispute, conflict, rift.

• Other antonym pairs testing similar ideas: Discord × Harmony, Enmity × Amity, Hostility × Friendliness.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
I don’t like being seen in tears by people.
option_1: I don’t like people had been seeing me in tears.
option_2: I don’t like people seeing me in tears.
option_3: I don’t like people to see me in tears.
option_4: I don’t like myself to be seen in tears.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. I don’t like people seeing me in tears.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "I don’t like being seen in tears by people" uses a passive gerund — "being seen... by people" — as the object of the verb "like".

• Rule — Converting a passive gerund to an active gerund:
◦ Passive gerund: being + V3 + by + agent
◦ Active gerund: agent + V-ing (gerund) + object

• Applying the rule: the agent "people" becomes the subject of the gerund phrase, and the verb "being seen" becomes "seeing", with "me" as its object; "in tears" remains as it is.
◦ Active: I don’t like people seeing me in tears.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "people had been seeing" introduces the Past Perfect Continuous tense, which changes the meaning and is not a correct active transformation of a passive gerund.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "people to see me" uses the infinitive "to see" instead of the required gerund "seeing" after the verb "like...being".

• Option 4 is incorrect because it changes the subject of the action from "people" to "myself", altering the meaning of the original sentence, which specifically refers to being seen by other people.

NOTE

• When a sentence has the structure "Subject + verb + being + V3 + by + agent", the active form always uses "agent + V-ing + object".

• Common verbs that take a gerund as object: like, dislike, enjoy, avoid, mind, finish, admit, deny, recall, resist.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Eat humble pie
option_3: To live a life of humility
option_4: To enjoy life to the fullest
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To apologise humbly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Eat humble pie" means to be forced to admit one’s mistake or defeat, and to apologise in a humiliating way. (विनम्रतापूर्वक माफी माँगना)
◦ Example: When his prediction turned out to be completely wrong, he had to eat humble pie in front of the whole team.

• The idiom originates from "umble pie", a pie made of the "umbles" (inferior entrails) of a deer, which servants ate while their masters ate the finest venison — hence, being made to eat it symbolised a lowering of status and a forced humility.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: To live in penury (गरीबी में जीना): To live in extreme poverty; unrelated to apologising.

• Option 3: To live a life of humility: Refers to a general humble lifestyle, not the specific act of apologising after being proven wrong.

• Option 4: To enjoy life to the fullest: Means to make the most of one’s life; this is unrelated to, and in fact opposite in tone to, the idiom.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to admitting fault often asked in SSC: "To eat one’s words" (to retract a statement), "To swallow one’s pride" (to act humbly despite injured pride), and "To bite the dust" (to fail or be defeated).

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence.
It is a deeply regrettable fact that deforestation has had a substantial consequenses on the environment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. consequenses.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "consequences" — results or effects, typically of an unwelcome nature, following an action or condition.
◦ Example: Deforestation has had a substantial consequence on the environment.

• Spelling key: the word ends in "-quences", not "-quenses" — it is built from con + sequence(s), and "sequence" is always spelt with a "c", never an "s", before the final "e".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "deforestation" is spelt correctly — the large-scale clearing of forests.

• Option 2: "substantial" is spelt correctly — of considerable size or importance.

• Option 3: "regrettable" is spelt correctly — deserving or causing regret; note the doubled "t".

NOTE

• Commonly confused pair: "sequence" (a c, not an s) versus words like "expense", where the sound is spelt with an "s" — always check whether a word is built from the root "sequence" (con-sequence, sub-sequent) before deciding the spelling.

• Other frequently misspelt words on this pattern: occurrence, existence, correspondence, maintenance.

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
option_1: Are you interested along with modern art?
option_2: Are you interested into modern art?
option_3: Are you interested with modern art?
option_4: Are you interested in modern art?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Are you interested in modern art?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "interested" is always followed by the preposition "in" when it refers to having curiosity or concern about a subject.
◦ Rule: interested + in + noun/gerund.
◦ Example: She has always been interested in classical music.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "interested along with" is not a valid collocation; "along with" means "together with" and does not fit after "interested".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "interested into" is grammatically wrong; "into" is used with verbs of motion or transformation, not with "interested".

• Option 3 is incorrect because "interested with" is not the correct preposition; "with" does not collocate with "interested" in this sense.

NOTE

• Other commonly tested adjective-preposition collocations: good at, afraid of, married to, proud of, angry with (a person)/at (a situation), keen on, fond of.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.
While I was travelling in Europe, I met a man who drew maps.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cartographer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Cartographer" is a person who draws or produces maps. (मानचित्रकार)
◦ Example: The cartographer spent months surveying the region before drawing the final map.

• The underlined phrase "man who drew maps" describes exactly this profession, so it is replaced by the single word "Cartographer".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Geographer (भूगोलवेत्ता): A person who studies the earth’s physical features, climate, and population — a broader field than just map-making.

• Option 3: Arbitrator (मध्यस्थ): A person appointed to settle a dispute between two parties; unrelated to maps.

• Option 4: Anthropologist (मानवविज्ञानी): A person who studies human societies and cultures; unrelated to maps.

NOTE

• Other commonly asked one-word substitutions for professions: Numismatist (one who studies/collects coins), Philatelist (one who collects stamps), Astronomer (one who studies celestial bodies), Archivist (one who maintains records/archives).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.
Scores given by the members are to be consolidated and sent in the head office immediately.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to the head office.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "send" is followed by the preposition "to" when it indicates the destination or direction towards which something is sent.
◦ Rule: send/sent + something + to + destination.
◦ Example: The report was sent to the head office for approval.

• In the given sentence, "the head office" is the destination to which the scores are being sent, so the underlined phrase "in the head office" must be corrected to "to the head office".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: No substitution is incorrect because "sent in the head office" is grammatically wrong; "in" does not indicate direction/destination.

• Option 2: "after the head office" is incorrect because "after" indicates time or sequence, not a destination.

• Option 3: "at the head office" is incorrect because "at" indicates a fixed location where an action happens, but "send" requires "to" to indicate the destination the scores are being moved towards.

NOTE

• Commonly confused prepositions with movement verbs: send/go/come/move + to (destination) versus stay/work/arrive + at (a point/location) versus live/be + in (an enclosed area).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Abominable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Admirable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Abominable" means causing disgust or hatred; extremely unpleasant or repugnant. (घृणित)
◦ Example: The abominable conditions in the camp shocked the visiting officials.

• Since abominable describes something that inspires disgust, its antonym must describe something that inspires respect and approval — "Admirable", meaning deserving admiration or respect. (प्रशंसनीय)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Worthy: Means deserving effort, attention, or respect in a general sense; it is a weaker, less precise opposite than "admirable" here.

• Option 2: Delectable (स्वादिष्ट): Means delicious or delightful, typically used for food; it is close in feel to "admirable" but is not the standard paired antonym of "abominable" and is more restricted to taste/pleasure.

• Option 4: Detestable: Means deserving intense dislike; this is a near-synonym of "abominable", not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Abominable": horrible, repulsive, loathsome, odious, vile.

• Commonly confused antonym pairs: Detestable × Admirable, Repugnant × Appealing, Odious × Delightful.

question: Select the sentences that contains no spelling errors.
option_1: I saw the dress catalouge pieces of Asha’s corchiture collection.
option_2: I saw the dress catalougue pieces of Asha’s couture collection.
option_3: I saw the dress catalougue pieces of Asha’s corchiture collection.
option_4: I saw the dress catalogue pieces of Asha’s couture collection.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I saw the dress catalogue pieces of Asha’s couture collection.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "catalogue" — a complete list of items, typically arranged systematically. Note the ending "-logue", not "-louge" or "-lougue".

• The correct spelling is "couture" — the design and manufacture of fashionable, made-to-measure clothing. Note it is spelt "cou-ture", not "cor-chiture".

• Option 4 is the only sentence in which both words — "catalogue" and "couture" — are spelt correctly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "catalouge" (should be "catalogue") and "corchiture" (should be "couture") are both misspelt.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "catalougue" (should be "catalogue") is misspelt, even though "couture" is spelt correctly.

• Option 3 is incorrect because both "catalougue" and "corchiture" are misspelt.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt French-origin fashion/business words: catalogue, couture, boutique, silhouette, connoisseur, cuisine.

• Memory tip: catalogue = cata + logue (like "dialogue", "monologue", "epilogue" — all end in "-logue").

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
After the government interventions, the enrolment and retention of female students have increased by leaps and bounds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Swiftly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "by leaps and bounds" means very rapidly; with great speed or in large increments. (तेज़ी से/द्रुत गति से)
◦ Example: Since the new policy was introduced, sales have grown by leaps and bounds.

• Since "swiftly" means quickly or rapidly, it is the closest match to the sense of rapid, large-scale progress conveyed by the idiom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Systematically: Means in a planned, methodical, step-by-step manner; this refers to the method of increase, not its speed, so it does not match the idiom.

• Option 3: Intermittently: Means occurring at irregular intervals, stopping and starting; this is nearly opposite to the idiom, which conveys continuous rapid growth.

• Option 4: Gradually: Means slowly, in small stages, over time; this is the opposite of the sense of rapid growth conveyed by "leaps and bounds".

NOTE

• Other idioms of rapid progress often asked in SSC: "At breakneck speed", "In the twinkling of an eye", and "Like wildfire" (to spread very quickly).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the collocation.
I had a nice ______ on my birthday with all my friends and relatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed collocation in English for enjoying an occasion is "have a nice/good time", meaning to enjoy oneself.
◦ Example: We had a nice time at the birthday party with all our friends and relatives.

• In the given sentence, the context of celebrating a birthday with friends and relatives fits precisely with the idiomatic collocation "a nice time".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "opportunity" does not collocate naturally with "nice" in this celebratory sense; one does not typically say "had a nice opportunity" for a birthday gathering.

• Option 2: "day" is grammatically possible but is a weaker, less idiomatic collocation here than "time", which specifically conveys enjoyment with people present.

• Option 3: "experience" can follow "nice" but usually describes a one-off encounter or event rather than the general enjoyment of a social occasion like a birthday celebration.

NOTE

• Other fixed collocations with "have": have a good time, have a great day, have a nice trip, have fun, have a blast.

question:
Select the correct passive voice form for the given sentence.
My brother likes cricket.
option_1: Cricket was like by my brother.
option_2: Cricket is like by my brother.
option_3: Cricket is liked by my brother.
option_4: Cricket was liked by my brother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cricket is liked by my brother.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "My brother likes cricket" is in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V1/V5 (likes) + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "cricket" becomes the subject; since it is singular/uncountable, the auxiliary used is "is"; the verb "likes" becomes the past participle "liked"; and "my brother" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: Cricket is liked by my brother.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "was like" is neither the correct tense (it wrongly uses the past auxiliary "was") nor the correct verb form (it should be the past participle "liked", not the base form "like").

• Option 2 is incorrect because "is like" incorrectly uses the base form "like" instead of the past participle "liked".

• Option 4 is incorrect because "was liked" is the passive form of the Simple Past Tense ("My brother liked cricket"), not the Simple Present Tense given in the question.

NOTE

• A very common error is using the base verb form (like) instead of the past participle (liked) in the passive; always check that the main verb is in its V3 (past participle) form.

• Other examples: He plays football → Football is played by him. She reads novels → Novels are read by her.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
He says to Gayatri, “You are writing an apology to the warden.”
option_1: He told Gayatri that she is writing an apology to the warden.
option_2: He tells Gayatri that she is writing an apology to the warden.
option_3: He says to Gayatri that she was writing an apology to the warden.
option_4: He tells Gayatri that she was writing an apology to the warden.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. He tells Gayatri that she is writing an apology to the warden.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reporting verb in the given sentence, "says to", is in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Reporting verb in the Present Tense: When the reporting verb is in the present tense, the tense of the reported speech does NOT change in indirect narration.
◦ Also, "says to" changes to "tells", and the conjunction "that" is added.
◦ Pronoun change: "you" in the direct speech (referring to Gayatri) changes to "she".

• Applying the rule: "says to" → "tells"; "You are writing" (Present Continuous) remains "she is writing" (Present Continuous, unchanged).
◦ Indirect: He tells Gayatri that she is writing an apology to the warden.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it uses "told", the past tense of the reporting verb, whereas the original reporting verb "says" is in the present tense and must remain unchanged.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it wrongly changes the reporting verb structure to "says to Gayatri that" — when reported indirectly, "says to" must become "tells", not remain as "says to...that" — and it also wrongly changes the tense to "was writing".

• Option 4 is incorrect because although it correctly uses "tells", it wrongly changes the reported verb to the Past Continuous "was writing", when it should remain in the Present Continuous "is writing" since the reporting verb is in the present tense.

NOTE

• Reporting verb changes: say to → tell; says → says/tells; the object is retained after "tell" but dropped after "say" (unless "say to" is used).

• Remember: tense backshift (e.g. present → past) in indirect speech applies only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
You must aware of friends who speak against you.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. beware of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aware" is an adjective and cannot directly follow a modal verb like "must" without a linking verb (e.g. "must be aware of"); the given sentence as written is therefore grammatically incorrect.

• "Beware" is a verb meaning to be cautious of, or careful to avoid, danger or a person, and it directly follows a modal verb like "must" without needing "be".
◦ Rule: must + beware of (verb), NOT must + aware of (adjective without a linking verb).
◦ Example: You must beware of strangers offering unsolicited advice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "caution of" is incorrect because "caution" as a verb takes the structure "caution someone against/about something", not "caution of".

• Option 3: "scarce of" is incorrect because "scarce" means insufficient in quantity and does not make sense in this context, nor is "scarce of" a standard construction.

• Option 4: "careful of" is grammatically valid on its own ("be careful of"), but after the modal "must" it would still require the linking verb "be" ("must be careful of"); "beware of" is the standard idiomatic verb used directly after a modal without "be".

NOTE

• Common confusion: "aware" (adjective, needs "be/become + aware of") versus "beware" (verb, used directly as "beware of").

• Other similar adjective-verb pairs tested in SSC: afraid (adj.) vs. fear (verb), conscious (adj.) vs. realise (verb).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in a sentence.
The good weather has been a boon for many businesses located near the beach.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. beneficial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "boon" means a thing or event that is helpful, welcome, and beneficial; something that brings advantage. (वरदान/लाभकारी वस्तु)
◦ Example: The new highway has been a boon for local traders, cutting travel time drastically.

• In the given sentence, "the good weather has been a boon for many businesses" means the good weather has been advantageous/beneficial for those businesses, so "beneficial" best captures this sense in context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "luck" refers to chance or fortune in a general sense, but it does not capture the specific idea of something being actively helpful or advantageous.

• Option 2: "Signal" means an indication or sign; it is unrelated to the meaning of "boon".

• Option 3: "fortune" can mean luck or wealth, but it does not specifically convey the sense of something being helpful or advantageous, which is the core meaning of "boon" here.

NOTE

• "Boon" is often contrasted with "bane", which means a cause of harm or misery — as in the common phrase "a boon or a bane".

• Other words meaning "advantageous/helpful": blessing, godsend, benefit, asset.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. While India is home to 75 per cent of tigers in the world, the Global Tiger Day – as it is also known – sees awareness events organised in the country, as well as neighbouring Bangladesh and Nepal.
B. Its primary objective is to preserve the natural habitat of the tiger.
C. International Tiger Day was initiated in 2010, at the Saint Petersburg Tiger Summit.
D. This annual event, observed on 29 July, aims to create awareness on tiger conservation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. CDBA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence C is the best opening sentence as it introduces the topic itself — "International Tiger Day was initiated in 2010..." — giving the name and origin of the event, which any coherent paragraph on this topic must begin with.

• Sentence D logically follows C, as it elaborates on C by giving further defining details — "This annual event, observed on 29 July..." — the pronoun-like reference "This annual event" directly points back to the day introduced in C.

• Sentence B follows next, continuing to describe the day’s "primary objective", building on the purpose ("aims to create awareness on tiger conservation") mentioned in D.

• Sentence A comes last, as it broadens the discussion to India’s specific context ("India is home to 75 per cent of tigers...") and mentions the observance events, forming a suitable concluding statement.
◦ Correct order: C → D → B → A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (DCAB) is incorrect because it starts with D, which refers back to "This annual event" — a phrase that requires the event to have already been introduced (as in C), so D cannot be the opening sentence.

• Option 2 (BADC) is incorrect because it starts with B, which refers to "Its primary objective" — the pronoun "Its" has no antecedent unless the event has already been named, so B cannot begin the paragraph.

• Option 4 (CDAB) is incorrect because although it correctly begins with C and D, placing A before B breaks the logical link between D’s mention of the day’s aim and B’s elaboration of "its primary objective", which must follow D directly.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always identify the sentence that introduces the subject/proper noun (here, "International Tiger Day") as it is almost always the opening sentence, since later sentences typically refer back to it using pronouns like "it", "its", or "this".

• Look for logical/pronoun linkages between sentences — a sentence using "its" or "this" must follow the sentence that first names the noun it refers to.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
One who runs away from law
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fugitive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Fugitive" is a person who has escaped from custody or is running away from the law, typically to avoid arrest or persecution. (फरार/भगोड़ा)
◦ Example: The fugitive was finally caught after evading the police for three years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Fatalist (भाग्यवादी): A person who believes that all events are predetermined by fate and therefore inevitable; unrelated to running from the law.

• Option 2: Convict (दोषी/सिद्धदोष): A person who has been found guilty of a crime and is serving, or has served, a sentence; this refers to someone already caught/convicted, not someone evading the law.

• Option 4: Lunatic (पागल): A person who is mentally ill or behaves in a wild, foolish way; unrelated to running from the law.

NOTE

• Other commonly asked one-word substitutes on this pattern: Vagabond (one who wanders with no fixed home), Deserter (one who abandons duty/military service), Absconder (one who is missing and evading legal proceedings) — often confused with "Fugitive".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Words that begin with the same letter, syllable or sound
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Alliteration.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Alliteration" is a literary device in which a series of words begin with the same letter, syllable, or sound. (अनुप्रास अलंकार)
◦ Example: "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers" is a classic example of alliteration.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Metaphor (रूपक): A figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to something it does not literally denote, to suggest a resemblance (e.g., "time is money"); unrelated to repeated sounds.

• Option 2: Pun (श्लेष): A play on words that exploits multiple meanings of a term, or similar-sounding words, for a humorous effect; not the same as repeating initial sounds.

• Option 3: Hyperbole (अतिशयोक्ति): A figure of speech involving deliberate exaggeration for emphasis (e.g., "I’ve told you a million times"); unrelated to repeated initial sounds.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused literary devices: Assonance (repetition of vowel sounds within nearby words), Onomatopoeia (words that imitate sounds, e.g. "buzz", "hiss"), Rhyme (repetition of similar sounds at the end of words).

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct collocation.
A gaggle of journalists sit in a/an _________ foyer waiting impatiently.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. hotel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "foyer" is an entrance hall or open area, typically found in buildings such as hotels, theatres, or large public buildings — it is not a feature of an attic, ranch, or croft.

• The natural, commonly used collocation is "hotel foyer", referring to the reception/entrance area of a hotel where guests or visitors wait.
◦ Example: The journalists gathered in the hotel foyer, waiting for the press conference to begin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "attic" refers to a room or space directly below the roof of a house, typically used for storage; an attic does not have a "foyer".

• Option 3: "ranch" refers to a large farm, especially one used for raising livestock such as cattle or horses; it does not have a "foyer" in common usage.

• Option 4: "croft" refers to a small enclosed field or a small rented farm, typically found in Scotland; it is far too small a structure to have a "foyer".

NOTE

• A "foyer" is typically associated with large, formal buildings: hotel foyer, theatre foyer, cinema foyer, office foyer.

• Collocation questions test which nouns naturally pair together in common usage — always picture the physical scale/type of place the word describes.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
Although Edward had noble blood, his ignoble qualities made him incapable of taking over the kingdom.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Unworthy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "ignoble" means not honourable in character or purpose; base, mean, or dishonourable. (नीच/अयोग्य/अशोभनीय)
◦ Example: His ignoble conduct towards his subjects cost him the respect of the entire court.

• "Unworthy" means lacking the qualities or character deserving of respect or a position, which closely matches the sense of "ignoble" in the sentence — Edward’s base/dishonourable qualities made him "unworthy" of the throne.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Salient: Means most noticeable or important; it does not carry any negative connotation of character, unlike "ignoble".

• Option 2: Strange: Means unusual or unfamiliar; it does not capture the specific sense of dishonourable or base character.

• Option 3: Ostentatious: Means designed to impress or attract notice, showy; this describes a manner of display, not a lack of honour or worthiness.

NOTE

• "Ignoble" is the antonym of "noble", and the sentence itself contrasts "noble blood" with "ignoble qualities" — a useful contextual clue.

• Other synonyms of "ignoble": base, dishonourable, contemptible, mean, shameful.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

At most of the local dhabas and fast food joints, poor hygienic conditions (1)__________. The (2)__________ occurs due to poor quality packaging material or (3)__________ storage conditions. Food cooked may not be washed or cleaned properly. It is low in (4)__________, rich in oil content especially trans fats which make one (5)__________, lousy and dull.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. prevail.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Prevail" means to exist or be widespread; to be the current or predominant state of affairs.
◦ Example: Poor hygienic conditions prevail in many small eateries that ignore basic sanitation norms.

• In the given sentence, the blank describes the general existence/widespread presence of "poor hygienic conditions" at dhabas and fast food joints, which is best expressed by "prevail".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "sustain" means to keep something going or support it over time; it does not fit the sense of a condition simply "existing" or being widespread.

• Option 3: "entail" means to involve or necessitate something as a consequence; it requires an object and does not fit grammatically or logically in this blank.

• Option 4: "assail" means to attack violently or criticise fiercely; it does not fit the context of describing existing conditions.

NOTE

• "Prevail" is commonly used to describe conditions, beliefs, or practices that are widespread in a place or at a time — e.g., "silence prevailed", "the custom still prevails in rural areas".

• Related word: "prevalent" (adjective) — widespread, common at a particular time.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

At most of the local dhabas and fast food joints, poor hygienic conditions (1)__________. The (2)__________ occurs due to poor quality packaging material or (3)__________ storage conditions. Food cooked may not be washed or cleaned properly. It is low in (4)__________, rich in oil content especially trans fats which make one (5)__________, lousy and dull.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. contamination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Contamination" means the process of making something impure or unsafe by exposing it to a poisonous or polluting substance.
◦ Example: Poor quality packaging material can lead to the contamination of food, making it unsafe to eat.

• The sentence describes how something negative "occurs due to poor quality packaging material" — the word must describe the harmful outcome of poor packaging on food, which is "contamination".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "perfection" means the state of being complete and flawless; this is the opposite of what poor packaging would cause, and does not fit the negative context.

• Option 3: "purification" means the process of removing impurities; this is also opposite in sense — poor packaging would cause impurity, not purification.

• Option 4: "concentration" means the state of being concentrated, or close attention to a task; it does not fit the context of a negative effect caused by poor packaging.

NOTE

• Words describing food safety issues often tested together: contamination, adulteration, spoilage, infestation.

• "Contaminate" (verb) → "contamination" (noun) → "contaminated" (adjective).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

At most of the local dhabas and fast food joints, poor hygienic conditions (1)__________. The (2)__________ occurs due to poor quality packaging material or (3)__________ storage conditions. Food cooked may not be washed or cleaned properly. It is low in (4)__________, rich in oil content especially trans fats which make one (5)__________, lousy and dull.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. unhygienic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unhygienic" means not clean or healthy; likely to cause disease due to lack of cleanliness.
◦ Example: Food stored in unhygienic storage conditions can quickly become unsafe to eat.

• The sentence lists causes of poor food quality — "poor quality packaging material or ___ storage conditions" — so the blank must describe storage conditions that are unclean/unsafe, matching the overall negative tone of the passage about poor hygiene.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "sterile" means completely free from bacteria or living microorganisms; this is a positive quality and contradicts the passage’s negative description of poor hygiene.

• Option 3: "neat" means clean, tidy, and orderly; this is also a positive quality that contradicts the context of poor hygienic conditions.

• Option 4: "energetic" means full of energy and enthusiasm; it does not describe a physical storage condition at all and is irrelevant here.

NOTE

• "Unhygienic" is the antonym of "hygienic" (clean, promoting health); the prefix "un-" negates the base word.

• Related words often tested together: sanitary × unsanitary, hygienic × unhygienic, clean × dirty/filthy.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

At most of the local dhabas and fast food joints, poor hygienic conditions (1)__________. The (2)__________ occurs due to poor quality packaging material or (3)__________ storage conditions. Food cooked may not be washed or cleaned properly. It is low in (4)__________, rich in oil content especially trans fats which make one (5)__________, lousy and dull.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. nutrition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nutrition" refers to the process of providing or obtaining the food necessary for health and growth; the nutrients/nutritional value contained in food.
◦ Example: Fast food is typically low in nutrition and high in unhealthy fats.

• The sentence contrasts being "low in ___" with being "rich in oil content", implying the blank should refer to something healthy or beneficial that the food lacks — "nutrition" fits this contrast perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "condition" is too vague and general in this context; it does not specifically capture the idea of nutritional value that pairs naturally with "rich in oil content".

• Option 2: "proportion" refers to a relative amount or ratio; it does not fit as something food can be described as being "low in" in this health-related context.

• Option 4: "production" refers to the process of making or manufacturing something; it is unrelated to the nutritional quality of food.

NOTE

• "Nutrition" (noun) → "nutritious" (adjective, meaning nourishing/healthy) → "nutrient" (a substance providing nourishment).

• Common contrast tested in SSC passages: food that is "low in nutrition" but "high/rich in fat, oil, or calories".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

At most of the local dhabas and fast food joints, poor hygienic conditions (1)__________. The (2)__________ occurs due to poor quality packaging material or (3)__________ storage conditions. Food cooked may not be washed or cleaned properly. It is low in (4)__________, rich in oil content especially trans fats which make one (5)__________, lousy and dull.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. obese.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Obese" means extremely overweight; having an excessive amount of body fat.
◦ Example: A diet rich in oil and trans fats, and low in nutrition, can make a person obese over time.

• The blank is grouped with the clearly negative words "lousy and dull", and follows a description of food that is "low in nutrition, rich in oil content especially trans fats" — such a diet is well known to cause excessive weight gain, making "obese" the fitting word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "smart" means clean, well-dressed, or intelligent; it is a positive word that does not fit alongside the negative words "lousy and dull".

• Option 2: "skinny" means very thin; a diet high in oil and trans fats and low in nutrition typically causes weight gain, not thinness, so this contradicts the logic of the passage.

• Option 4: "affluent" means having a great deal of money; it is unrelated to the physical effects of an unhealthy diet described in the passage.

NOTE

• A diet "low in nutrition" and "rich in trans fats" is a classic description used in SSC passages to lead into words like obese, unhealthy, lethargic.

• Related words: obesity (noun), overweight, corpulent (all describing excess body weight).
